question: Can an LLM judge be trusted to grade agent output?

sides.stance: Yes, once the evaluator has been evaluated until it agrees with human judgment on golden datasets.
Yes, as short markdown rubrics with pass/fail thresholds applied to each conversation.
No: LLM verdicts change across identical replications and when challenged, so they are unreliable verifiers.
No: LLM-as-judge scoring proved too noisy to rely on; redesign the agent so it can be evaluated by construction.

question: Should a human approve agent actions before they take effect?

sides.stance: Yes: agents propose actions with scoped identity and least privilege, and a human approves before anything changes.
No: approving every action causes review fatigue; deterministic rules and classifiers handle routine calls and escalate only ambiguous ones.
Only at one irreducible step: the human watches each feature video and understands the PR.

question: Should agent reliability live in the harness or be absorbed into the model?

sides.stance: Newer models score about the same in any harness, so harness scaffolding no longer adds coding intelligence and the model absorbs it.
Builders must encode opinionated process around the agent, because open-ended agents produce inconsistent results.
In each new domain the harness has to re-add prompting and guardrails until the model masters those tasks.

question: Should enterprises build on owned open foundations or on the frontier labs' stack?

sides.stance: Whatever platform roots a company's agentic processes hardens into its organization, so it should be an open foundation the company controls.
Model capability is no longer the constraint; the opportunity is a reusable agent foundation built on frontier models.
Going a layer below the frontier APIs pays now rather than waiting for the labs.
